purpose: Reusable implementation context for HC-106 database bootstrap and test identity support.
Helps future agents avoid re-discovery of the current auth contract, startup seams, and tester workflow gap.
non_goals: Changing server identity persistence or storage/server_identity.json handling.
Implementing HC-107 startup preflight or broader failure messaging.
Designing a full migration framework unless that is proven to be the smallest viable path.
Broadening auth beyond the current nickname lookup contract without concrete code evidence.

conventions: Use tabs, OTBS braces, descriptive camelCase, and Odin naming conventions from AGENTS.md.
Server validation commands are odin check server and odin test server from server/AGENTS.md.
Keep edits minimal and focused on HC-106 only.
Use Odin tests where practical and prefer additive changes over wider architecture changes.

hard: Current confirmed auth contract is nickname lookup in server/database.odin using SELECT id::text FROM users WHERE nickname = $1 LIMIT 1.
No checked-in schema, bootstrap, or seed path currently exists.
Testers must not need manual SQL for the supported auth setup flow.
soft: Prefer the current local helper path instead of inventing multiple new entrypoints.
Keep schema and seed scope to the minimum required MVP auth records.
Avoid coupling HC-106 to future preflight or packaging work beyond what the acceptance criteria require.
compatibility: server/main.odin validates nickname length 3..32 before dispatching AuthLookupByNickname database work.
server/router_test.odin already asserts auth lookup messages are forwarded as structured database requests.
run-test-server.sh already sets local log and storage paths plus a database password default, so it is the clearest existing tester helper seam.
security_requirements: Do not commit secrets or API keys.
Use environment variables for sensitive database connection inputs.
Validate all bootstrap inputs and keep seeded data limited to non-sensitive test identities.
Prefer idempotent setup to reduce risky manual database intervention.

patterns: server/database.odin is the single confirmed database execution surface and currently offers raw SQL plus structured auth lookup requests.
server/config.odin owns environment-driven runtime configuration and storage path normalization.
run-test-server.sh is a thin local launcher that already exports tester-local defaults before odin run server.
Router tests use an in-process IPC harness with focused assertions instead of full PostgreSQL integration.

gotchas.text: There is no existing migration or seed framework to extend, so file placement and invocation must be chosen deliberately.
Current tests stub database IPC rather than exercise a live database, so fresh-environment bootstrap validation may need one narrow new command-path check.
run-test-server.sh currently defaults only logs, storage path, and database password; it does not provision database state.

security_considerations.concern: Bootstrap support must continue to rely on environment variables for secrets and avoid checked-in credentials beyond existing local defaults.
Only non-sensitive test identities should be seeded, and the flow should be safe to rerun locally.

domain_context.error_handling: Database worker returns structured DatabaseQueryResponse errors; router path sends explicit auth lookup failure payloads for invalid input.
domain_context.data_flow: ClientAuthLookup nickname -> server/main structured DatabaseQueryRequest.AuthLookupByNickname -> server/database SQL lookup on users.nickname -> string user ID result.

open_questions.question: Is the smallest supported bootstrap flow code-owned in the database worker or shell-owned using checked-in SQL assets?
open_questions.context: Both are plausible from current seams, but only one should be blessed to minimize blast radius.

prior_decisions.decision: Keep HC-106 scoped to the current nickname lookup contract unless stronger schema requirements are proven during execution.
rationale: Code evidence only proves users.nickname to id lookup today.
The user requested MVP-only scope and minimal blast radius.
